source.snippet: At off peak pricing, which is substantially lower than the standard API rate (50% off). So I assume it looks even better financially overall. Quick numbers: At $35/hour in net cash generation per card, a $30,000 GPU would pay for itself entirely in about 850 hours (roughly 35 days). With an assumed ~$3 operation cost per card and hour.

problem_statement: Operators running LLM inference commercially lack simple tools to model GPU ROI, optimal pricing tiers (peak vs. off-peak), and break-even timelines before committing to $30k+ hardware purchases.
target_segment: Independent LLM inference operators and small AI hosting businesses considering on-premise GPU investment
notes: Buyer signal: commenter is calculating commercial returns at $35/hr net per card against a $30k hardware cost — clearly an operator or prospective operator, not a hobbyist. Willingness to invest at $30k+ hardware scale implies a paid-tooling budget. Only one data point so signal_strength capped at 2; worth watching for cluster growth.
